medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Baccalaureate MD Program is a pre-matriculation program open to undergraduate students from disadvantaged backgrounds.  https://www.umassmed.edu/baccmd 
Please visit our website to learn more.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A student in good academic standing may request a leave of absence for a specified period of time not to exceed one year. The request must be made in writing to the Associate Dean for Student Affairs, who will bring the request to the appropriate Academic Evaluation Board for consideration. The appropriate Academic Evaluation Board will determine whether or not such a leave of absence is to be granted, whether or not it can be renewed, and what, if any, conditions for readmission will be set.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Recognizing that the most effective physicians are well rounded individuals, we offer a variety of optional activities outside of the formal curriculum. Student interest groups run the gamut from community service in Free Clinic programs and other service opportunities both in the local community and internationally.  In addition, UMass Chan has a unique program of not for credit Optional Enrichment Electives. Many of the electives are student initiated, which allow students to explore a gamut of interests from creative writing to health care policy.  Students are members of Learning Communities, established to allow more interclass interaction where students can learn from each other.  All entering first-year students are assigned to one of six houses.  These social and academic homes are overseen by faculty mentors, who act as advisors, teachers and career development coaches.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: UMass Chan is in Worcester, MA in central Massachusetts. UMass Memorial Health Care is the clinical partner of UMass Chan and the largest health care system serving central and western Massachusetts. The medical school and clinical affiliate share adjoining buildings. There are numerous institutions of higher learning in the area offering culturally diverse activities. The campus is accessible by local bus, rideshare and taxicab services.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is not available. There are many affordable apartments near the medical school. Rents average $1400-$2000 per month.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The UMass Chan Diversity and Inclusion Office provides support for students who identify as gender or sexual minorities. QMass is a student interest group committed to making UMass Chan a more LGBTQIA+-friendly place for students, patients, and community members. We strive to provide resources and community events to build connections, raise awareness, and promote the well-being and acceptance of LGBTQIA+ individuals both within and connected with UMass Chan.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
As part of our commitment to diversity, UMass Chan seeks to attract and educate students and trainees who will make the population of health care professionals representative of the national population. We are, therefore, committed to the full and meaningful inclusion of qualified students, trainees, and employees with disabilities in all programs and activities.  Reasonable accommodations when requested by qualified students/learners will be supported through our accommodation request process.

Support for students/learners include, but are not limited to
Exam accommodations
Classroom accommodations
Clerkship accommodations
Assistive technology
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Students are encouraged to actively pursue positive and mindful experiences that foster multi-dimensional well-being as part of a well-rounded lifestyle aimed at promoting resilience and success within their medical education and beyond. There are several resources offered to students to ensure a balance of academic, community, physical and emotional wellness. 
Please visit our website to learn more: https://www.umassmed.edu/studentlife/wellness/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
At UMass Chan, it’s not just what we do.
It’s how we do it—together.

Training the next generation of world-class physicians, scientists and advanced practice nurses. Forming unconventional partnerships that lead to groundbreaking research and clinical trials. Reaching out and working within our communities to make them healthier and improve lives.

We do this work daily, proudly, within a unique culture not found anywhere else.

Many great minds.
One UMass Chan.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: All T.H. Chan School of Medicine students are required to have access to their own transportation while in school. Hospital rotations will occur throughout the city of Worcester and State of Massachusetts with limited public transportation available.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: During the clinical years, and in any patient encounters during the preclinical years students are expected to dress professionally
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Asst. Dean for Academic Achievement directs the learning skills program which is open to all students at UMass Chan, including academic counseling, tutoring and a series of learning seminars.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin seeing patients with a Longitudinal Preceptor from the first weeks of school through fall of the 2nd year. They begin seeing hospitalized patients in the winter of their first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Curriculum includes lecture, small group sessions (case-based, problem-based learning etc.), lab, simulation (standardized patient and high fidelity) and applied knowledge conference sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clerkship experiences are divided into 4 12-week integrated units including: OBGYN/Pediatrics, Medicine, Surgery/Radiology, Mind/Brain/Behavior with a longitudinal Family Medicine Clerkship Experience
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are not ranked, but a committee meets to review overall performance..
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Class attendance is strongly recommended. Lecture recordings are offered as a learning resource. Attendance may be required at the discretion of the faculty.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Vista Curriculum incorporates innovations in teaching, learning and new national standards for medical education. The UMass Chan educational program prepares students for their future medical careers regardless of specialty choice, while maintaining our founding commitment to prepare students for training in the primary care disciplines. Our curriculum comprises the three pillars of biomedical, clinical and health systems sciences.  It emphasizes early patient exposure; strong clinical skills development; problem solving and professionalism; student activism in community service; diverse opportunities for research and promotion of life-long learning skills.  Learning communities, which bring together small groups of students and faculty across class years for formal and informal teaching and mentoring, are a featured highlight of our comprehensive curriculum design. Educational methods promote interactive learning, with hands-on practice under the close observation of faculty.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: UMass Chan and its network of affiliated institutions have developed long-standing and respected primary care educational programs. These programs provide students with opportunities to experience generalist practice in a full spectrum of settings, including large group practices, community health centers and private practices - each with a significant managed care component. Programs sponsored by UMass Chan and its partners have also demonstrated a strong commitment to the underserved in both urban and rural sectors of the state. The UMass Chan-Baystate PURCH track is a parallel educational program that seeks to recruit students with a strong interest in primary care serving rural and urban underserved populations. The Center for the Advancement of Primary Care (CAPC) at UMass Chan and UMass Memorial Health has a mission to strengthen and enhance the valuable primary care network existing throughout the UMass Memorial system.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Senior Scholars Research, Independent Research/Study and International Research electives available.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: UMass Chan is committed to training physicians in a range of medical disciplines and emphasizes training for practice in general medicine and the primary care specialties in the public sector and in underserved areas of Massachusetts. This mission has since been expanded to include graduate education in the biomedical sciences and nursing, graduate medical education, and continuing medical education for health professionals. The school's clinical partner is UMass Memorial Medical Center, consisting of two acute care hospitals and a regional hospital with a total of 800 beds. Clinical education is also conducted at a number of affiliated community hospitals and health centers in the region.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The mission of UMass Chan Medical School is to advance the health and well-being of the people of the commonwealth and the world through pioneering advances in education, research and health care delivery. 

The UMass Chan Medical School Office of Admissions is committed to employing the most effective and evidence-based methods to recruit and matriculate future physicians and scientists who will provide the highest quality medical care for our communities in keeping with the mission of the T.H. Chan School of Medicine.  Our graduates will contribute in a meaningful way to the elimination of health care disparities and the establishment of health equity in Massachusetts and beyond.
 
Our Office of Admissions advances the mission of UMass Chan by applying a mission aligned review process to every eligible application. We place the highest value on applicant characteristics that reflect our institutional commitments such as commitment to health equity, diversity and inclusion, and service to the community.
 
Our VISTA curriculum has an innovative, integrated structure based on foundational, clinical and health systems sciences. The longitudinal focus topics of health equity, societal forces in health and disease and health systems science are woven into all courses and rotations. At UMass Chan, we believe that patients are whole people, not just a collection of organ systems, and must be seen in the context of their lives. Student and health care provider wellness is highly prioritized as evidenced by the “WIN” week which appears at the end of each foundational block. WIN stands for “What I Need” and is an opportunity for students to rest, focus on health and expose themselves to educational enrichment.    

Our clinical training sites are located across the commonwealth with housing provided where indicated, offering a rich clinical training experience for our learners.  In the Exploration Phase, students participate in 12-week integrated units that ensure exposure to inpatient and ambulatory environments in both acute care and chronic disease management.  Our Horizons phase focuses on advanced clinical skills and preparation for residency. 

A unique feature of the VISTA curriculum which is closely aligned with the UMass Chan mission is our pathways. At the main campus in Worcester MA, students will select a pathway for educational focus during their early clinical learning time. These pathways range from “Entrepreneurship Biomedical Innovation and Design” to “Structural Inequity, Advocacy and Justice”. There are two UMass Chan Medical School regional campuses each with their own pathway focus. At our PURCH program at Baystate Health systems, students focus on Population-based Urban and Rural Community Health. Our LEAD@Lahey program at Lahey Health focuses on leadership, innovation, and Health Systems Science. The T.H. Chan School of Medicine mission is woven into everything we do.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
The letters section of your application will be marked complete upon receipt of all letters listed in your AMCAS application. Letters that are listed in your AMCAS application but are not received will result in an incomplete application.

If you are no longer submitting a letter listed in your application, please contact AMCAS for guidance on how to void the letter and contact UMass Chan's office of Admissions.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
A composite premed committee letter is expected when available.
If a pre-med committee letter is not available, please submit letters from two science professors. 
~Additional letters should come from mentors, advisors and supervisors from academic, research, employment, volunteer and service opportunities.
~Letters from family members and friends are not recommended.
~If you are enrolled in or have completed a post baccalaureate or graduate program in biomedical sciences, a letter from the program director is expected in lieu of the undergraduate letter requirements.
~If you are applying to the MD/PhD program, please provide letters from a minimum of two most recent research supervisors for a maximum of five letters.  Applicants may exceed the six letter maximum if the additional letters are from research supervisors
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Interviews are by invitation of the Admissions Committee only. Applicants will be able to select their preferred interview time via the PeopleSoft system following receipt of an interview invitation. PURCH Track, LEAD@Lahey track and MD/PhD applicants will select from a bundle of interview options as there are separate interviews for PURCH, LEAD@Lahey and MD/PhD applicants. If an MD/PhD applicant is also applying to the PURCH track, that applicant will be selecting a bundle with three separate interviews.

Applicants will be provided access to orientation videos outlining the MMI, our admissions process, curriculum and financial aid prior to their interview date. Details and access to any virtual sessions will be accessible within PeopleSoft.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Applications to the MD and combined MD/PhD programs are open to both Massachusetts residents and non-residents. Approximately 35% of each incoming first-year class is composed of non-Massachusetts residents. Eligible applicants include U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, individuals with DACA status, and U.S. asylees or refugees. All non-citizens must provide official documentation of their immigration status. Immigration cases must be fully adjudicated with a positive outcome, and applicants must submit documentation verifying this status.

Prospective applicants who are awaiting final decisions on their permanent residency applications are not eligible to apply unless their current immigration status is DACA, refugee, or asylee. If an applicant does not hold one of these statuses but is granted permanent residency before the application deadline, they are welcome to apply. All application materials—including MCAT and PREview scores, and proof of immigration status—must be submitted by the published deadline.

The only international applicants eligible to apply currently are Canadian citizens and Canadian permanent residents. Canadian applicants must provide official proof of citizenship or permanent residency.
Eligible applicants who have graduated from an international college or university must complete at least one full year of coursework in the biomedical sciences at an accredited U.S. or Canadian institution before applying to the T.H. Chan School of Medicine. Please refer to the T.H. Chan School of Medicine Admissions Requirements website for additional information.

Applicants currently enrolled in a professional or graduate program must be in the terminal year of their degree program to be considered for admission. Applicants are expected to complete the academic program in which they are enrolled at any time during the application process and prior to possible matriculation at the T.H. Chan School of Medicine.

https://www.umassmed.edu/som/admissions/apply/academic-requirements/

We strongly prefer that prerequisite courses be completed at an applicant’s home undergraduate institution during the standard academic semesters and taken for a letter grade. Exceptions may be made for extenuating circumstances—for example, when online coursework was required due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Applicants should provide an explanation in their application for any deviations from these expectations or from other stated application protocols.

Secondary applications must be submitted by December 1, 2026. This deadline includes the submission of MCAT and PREview scores. PREview is required for all applicants including those applying to the MSTP (MD/PhD) program and cannot be substituted with CASPer.

Applicants are expected to provide committee letters when this is available to them.  We will accept individual letters when premed committee letters are not available from the applicant's institution.

Individuals who have previously matriculated at another medical school are not eligible to apply to the T.H. Chan School of Medicine other than through the transfer process in the clinical year, and only if there is space in the class and the applicant meets the transfer requirements. 

https://www.umassmed.edu/som/admissions/apply/transfer-to-school/
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The preference is for required courses to be completed at a four-year university or college.  Community college coursework is accepted on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Updates are welcome if they detail information that was not originally provided in the AMCAS application and relay accomplishments or achievements that were attained post application submission.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Applicants who meet the academic criteria and are able to meet the School’s Technical Standards, with or without reasonable accommodations, consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) will be considered for admission. Applicants with questions about whether they can meet these standards are encouraged to review them with their healthcare providers before applying.

The use of a human intermediary to meet the Technical Standards—when such assistance would substitute for a student’s own judgment, observation, or interpretation—is not permitted. Reliance on another person’s abilities in this way is inconsistent with the requirement that students independently meet the Technical Standards of the T.H. Chan School of Medicine.  A student must possess the aptitude, abilities, and skills in these five areas:

Observation
Communication
Sensory and Motor Coordination
Intellectual‑Conceptual, Integrative, and Quantitative Abilities
Professionalism: Behavioral and Social Attributes

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Our MD/MBA is a program with the opportunity to pursue a dual degree from UMass Chan and UMass Lowell.

Population-based Urban and Rural Community Health (PURCH) Track:  UMass Chan has partnered with our regional campus UMass Chan -Baystate in Springfield, MA to offer a 4-year track toward a medical degree for students wishing to focus on rural and urban primary care and population health.  For more information:
https://www.umassmed.edu/som/academics/purch-track/

LEAD@Lahey Track: The innovative LEAD@Lahey (LEAD = lead, empower, advocate, deliver) track is hosted at our regional medical school campus, in partnership with Lahey Hospital & Medical Center (Lahey), a part of Beth Israel Lahey Health (BILH), in Burlington, MA. Students on this track will follow the core curriculum of the T.H. Chan School of Medicine at UMass Chan Medical School with an added focus on leadership, health systems science and interprofessional education.
https://www.umassmed.edu/som/academics/umass-chan-lahey/

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
As our curriculum evolves we find students benefit from successfully completing courses in social sciences, statistics and biochemistry.  Community college courses for meeting prerequisite requirements are accepted but not recommended.  Applicants are strongly encouraged to complete pre-requisite coursework in a classroom based setting at their bachelor degree granting institution.  
Explanations can be provided on the Secondary Application regarding your academic background.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Recommended completion within the last six years. Review our website for more information: https://www.umassmed.edu/som/admissions/apply/academic-requirements/
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Acceptance decisions depend on mission-aligned review of the following:   
Prior academic performance.
MCAT scores.
Service and extracurricular achievements which indicate an ability to work with people in a helping role. 
A bachelor's degree from a U.S. or Canadian accredited undergraduate school.
Attributes that contribute to the diversity of the class, including, but not limited to, socio-economic background, cultural awareness, work experience, languages spoken, gender, gender identity, and sexual orientation. Also considered in diversity are students from disadvantaged backgrounds and resiliency in terms of positive capacity to cope with stress and adversity.
Oral, written, and interpersonal skills as documented in letters of support and in the interview.
Attributes and values deemed necessary for physicians including honesty, altruism, compassion, maturity, self-awareness, ability for self-directed learning and ability to work as a member of a team.
